items.name: System Diagnostics & Scanning
items.desc: Real-time monitoring of data lines and flows, active fault code detection, and restoration of vehicle communication networks.
items.longDesc: Real-time monitoring of data lines and flows, active fault code detection, and restoration of vehicle communication networks — we find the root cause before touching a single part, and explain it before we quote.
paragraphs: Before we touch a single part, we connect the vehicle or machine to multi-brand scan equipment to read active and pending fault codes, review live data streams, and isolate whether the problem sits in a sensor, a module, or the communication network (CAN, J1939). This avoids the most expensive mistake in diesel mechanics: swapping parts by trial and error.

A typical case: a truck with an intermittent check-engine light. Instead of assuming it's the most common sensor, we compare ECM data streams against manufacturer-expected values and confirm the root cause before quoting any part — often the problem is a corroded connector or a loose ground, not the sensor itself.
signals: Fault code report with date, mileage, and root cause

items.name: Electrical Problem Solving
items.desc: Tracing and repair of short circuits, advanced alternator, connector, sensor, and automotive & industrial relay diagnostics.
items.longDesc: Tracing and repair of short circuits, plus advanced diagnostics of alternators, connectors, sensors, and automotive & industrial relays, with documented circuit verification before delivery.
paragraphs: We trace short circuits and intermittent faults with a multimeter and system-specific wiring diagrams, not by guesswork — confirming with data whether the issue is the alternator, a corroded connector, a sensor, or a relay before disassembling anything.

On industrial equipment and commercial fleets, a misdiagnosed electrical fault often comes back within days. That's why we leave documented circuit verification — voltage, continuity, and load — before handing the unit back.
signals: Multimeters and oscilloscope for intermittent faults
Wiring diagrams by make and model

items.name: High-Pressure Hydraulic Systems
items.desc: Diagnostics and repair of leaks in lines, hoses, pressure pumps, hydraulic cylinders, valves, and heavy equipment control systems.
items.longDesc: Diagnostics and repair of leaks in lines, hoses, pressure pumps, hydraulic cylinders, valves, and heavy equipment control systems — stable pressure, no leaks, load-tested before handover.
paragraphs: We diagnose leaks and pressure loss in lines, hoses, pumps, cylinders, and valves on heavy equipment — identifying whether the cause is a worn seal, fluid contamination, or a valve that isn't cycling correctly.
After the repair we test the system under real load, not just idle: that's the only way to confirm pressure stays stable through the machine's actual duty cycle before it goes back into operation.
signals: Pressure gauges and hydraulic test equipment

items.name: Fleet General Mechanics
items.desc: Corrective and preventive mechanical services for heavy-duty diesel trucks, gasoline and utility vehicles.
items.longDesc: Corrective and preventive mechanical services for heavy-duty diesel trucks, gasoline and utility vehicles, with a service record per vehicle and contract-based maintenance windows.
paragraphs: We cover corrective and preventive maintenance for heavy-duty diesel trucks, gasoline vehicles, and utility vehicles — keeping a service history per unit so the fleet has real traceability, not just loose invoices.
We coordinate contract-based maintenance windows with the fleet coordinator to minimize downtime, and hand back every vehicle with a report and photos of the work done.

items.name: On-Site Mobile Support
items.desc: Deployment of fully equipped mobile units with advanced tools to solve technical issues in hard-to-access work areas or remote projects.
items.longDesc: Deployment of fully equipped mobile units with advanced tools to solve technical issues in hard-to-access work areas or remote projects: the shop comes to where your equipment operates.
paragraphs: We deploy fully equipped mobile units with diagnostic and repair tools to work on machinery and fleets directly on-site — at a job site, a yard, or wherever the equipment is down — without hauling it to a shop.

This matters most for heavy equipment that's hard to move, or projects on a tight schedule: the goal is to fix the fault on-site and get the equipment back in production the same day whenever possible.
signals: Mobile units with diagnostic and repair tools
On-site service at job sites, yards, or remote locations
Priority: equipment running again the same day

items.name: Roadside Mechanical Assistance
items.desc: Rapid response on highways and transport routes to minimize commercial vehicle and heavy equipment downtime.
items.longDesc: Rapid response on highways and transport routes to minimize commercial vehicle and heavy equipment downtime. One goal: getting your operation moving again.
paragraphs: We respond on highways and transport routes when a commercial vehicle or heavy equipment goes down — the goal is to fix it on the spot or get the unit into a safe condition for towing, minimizing downtime.
We coordinate directly with the driver or fleet coordinator to confirm location, fault type, and priority, and roll out with the tools needed based on the initial reported diagnosis.

items.name: Salvage & Component Recovery
items.desc: Recovery, disassembly and evaluation of parts and reusable components to reduce costs and extend the useful life of equipment.
items.longDesc: Recovery, disassembly and evaluation of parts and reusable components to reduce costs and extend the useful life of equipment — value recovered from machines others would write off.
paragraphs: We disassemble and evaluate parts and components from decommissioned or out-of-service equipment to determine which ones are still functional — a real alternative to buying new when a recovered component does the same job.
Every recovered part is tested before it's reused or sold; this cuts maintenance costs for fleets running older equipment and extends the useful life of machines that would otherwise be scrapped.
signals: Applies to older or discontinued equipment
